original_purpose: Independence and confidentiality of persons exercising sponsor reserved (A3+) authority
problem: One-sponsor exclusivity turns every routine decider and December surge reviewer into a per-sponsor fixed cost; with 5 sponsors the decider bench is ~5x a pooled bench
proposed_replacement: Allow a person to be appointed by several sponsor boards for routine decision classes (eligibility exceptions within policy, renewals) with per-sponsor appointment, tenant-scoped sessions, conflict attestations, per-sponsor decision caps and sampled cross-sponsor quality review; keep exclusivity for discretionary holds, reconsideration and anything touching related-party or §4958 signals
economic_implication: Bench sized by total workload, not sponsor count; at R the December decider bench falls from ~5 to ~2 people [E]
operational_implication: One queue across sponsors; needs conflict register
security_implication: Cross-tenant access risk; mitigated by per-item authentication (CNV-TEN-001)
financial_control_implication: Each decision remains under one sponsor's recorded authority and §4966(d)(3) fund-manager list
acceptance_criteria: Given a reviewer appointed by sponsors S1 and S2, when they open an S2 item, then the session authenticates into S2's cell only and the decision record names S2's appointment; and a quarterly sample shows decision quality at or above single-sponsor reviewers
remaining_uncertainty: Sponsor boards' and counsel's acceptance; owner kept the absolute rule for release 1
legal_obligation_preserved: yes: §4966 fund-manager status and sponsor control unchanged
relation_to_prior_candidates: extends RC-ACT-002 / RC-SE-005 (which pooled only non-deciders)

original_purpose: Segregation of duties for payment release
problem: Until auditor and board acceptance, the three-distinct-person rule requires three humans per release chain, which fixes a minimum staff floor and slows straight-through grants
problem_category: creates recurring human work; prevents workload-driven operations
proposed_replacement: Make the auditor acceptance package (policy approval evidence, ITGC design, negative SoD tests, deterministic gate test results) a deliverable of onboarding; during the interim allow two humans plus the engine-enforced gate when 100% of gate-released items are post-reviewed within 2 business days, until acceptance or 90 days
economic_implication: Removes one person from each release chain during pre-acceptance (~$99k/yr at R) [D]
security_implication: None weakened if post-review is complete and timely
financial_control_implication: Detects rather than prevents during interim; post-review must be able to recall/hold before settlement for ACH next-day
acceptance_criteria: Given an interim sponsor, when a gate-released item is not post-reviewed within 2 business days, then new releases stop for that sponsor; and the external auditor's written planned approach is recorded before interim ends
remaining_uncertainty: Whether auditors accept detective interim controls

problem: Gate requires pre-contracted, pre-appointed surge reviewers before 1 December even when simulated peak meets every legal deadline with deferral
proposed_replacement: Readiness gate passes on a simulated-peak plan that meets every legal deadline (contribution dating, acknowledgments, sanctions-before-release) using the deferral policy and pooled queue; contracted surge reviewers required only where simulation shows a legal-deadline or contractual SLA miss
economic_implication: Avoids a standby bench per sponsor; prior study: 10 vs 5.7 ops FTE-equivalents at 5,000 accounts in December
operational_implication: Requires published December SLA (up to 10 business days)
acceptance_criteria: Given the simulation at k=3 and k=5 arrivals, when deferral is applied, then zero legal deadlines are missed and the contractual December SLA is met; else the gate requires named surge reviewers
legal_obligation_preserved: yes: no December 31 legal deadline for DAF grant payment

original_purpose: Human work orchestration with clear case ownership
problem: Queues are sponsor-scoped with cradle-to-grave ownership defaults, which presumes a team per sponsor and prevents a servicer from routing work by skill and load across sponsors
proposed_replacement: Make the federated cross-tenant queue (routing metadata only, CNV-TEN-001) the default for an Administrator principal, with skill/load-based assignment across sponsors and per-item authentication; sponsor-scoped queues remain for sponsors that self-operate
economic_implication: Utilisation-safe pooling; fewer idle hours per sponsor [E]
operational_implication: One work list, workload metrics per sponsor for billing
security_implication: No PII in shared queue store (unchanged)
acceptance_criteria: Given 5 sponsors, when items arrive, then assignment uses skill and load across sponsors and each item's record shows the sponsor delegation used; shared store contains only case id, kind, priority, due time, sponsor id

original_purpose: Evidence that the sponsor exercises variance power and exclusive legal control over delegated automation
problem: 12-month delegation expiry and refusal to renew after one unacknowledged quarterly report create a cliff back to pre-delegation operation (three-person release, per-grant decisions)
problem_category: creates recurring human work; prevents workload-driven operations
proposed_replacement: Delegation continues until revoked; annual re-adoption bundled with the board's annual policy review; an unacknowledged quarterly report triggers escalation and an automatic narrowing (lower auto-approval ceiling) after 30 days rather than lapse
economic_implication: Avoids reversion cost (~$0.94M/yr at R if all sponsors revert to AI-enhanced handling [M])
financial_control_implication: Control evidence of oversight preserved; narrowing is fail-safe
acceptance_criteria: Given an unacknowledged report at day 30, then the ceiling drops to the sponsor-set fallback and the board chair is notified; given no annual re-adoption by month 13, then the delegation lapses
remaining_uncertainty: Counsel view on whether continuous delegation evidences exclusive legal control
legal_obligation_preserved: yes: legal control remains with the sponsor board

problem: Quarterly workforce and annual delegated-customer (advisor, viewer) recertification create recurring human tasks, part of which is transferred to donors and advisors
proposed_replacement: Event-driven recertification (role change, termination feed, inactivity >90 days auto-suspend, risk signal) with continuous entitlement analytics; keep quarterly evidence for privileged roles; replace annual advisor recertification by inactivity expiry and notification
economic_implication: Removes most donor/advisor recertification contacts [E]
security_implication: Better: revocation is immediate instead of periodic
acceptance_criteria: Given an advisor inactive for 90 days, then access is suspended and a self-service reactivation with step-up is offered; privileged-role quarterly review evidence is generated
remaining_uncertainty: Auditor acceptance of event-driven model for non-privileged roles

original_purpose: Monitor vendor SOC report coverage and bridge-letter gaps
problem: Release 1 performs this as an annual manual review; gaps between annual reviews go undetected
problem_category: prevents automated control evidence; creates recurring human work
proposed_replacement: Ship the small data model in release 1: report periods, relying-party year-ends, gap computation, alerts at 3 and 12 months; manual review only on exceptions
economic_implication: Small build (<2 engineer-weeks [E]); removes annual review hours
acceptance_criteria: Given a vendor SOC report ending 31 March and a relying party year-end 31 December, then a bridge-letter task opens at the configured gap and the record shows the computation inputs

original_purpose: Assurance scope set by actual reliance; avoid premature SOC cost
problem: Manual review procedures may be replaced by generated evidence only after the auditor confirms reliance, so the first year(s) run manual procedures in parallel with the automation that exists
problem_category: prevents automated control evidence; creates recurring human work
proposed_replacement: Allow generated evidence with information-produced-by-entity support (query, parameters, counts, hash, run log) from inception, run in parallel with a sampled manual check (not full manual procedure) until the auditor confirms reliance; define the SOC 1 boundary per layer (servicing processes + platform ITGCs, inclusive method for Unbound if separate)
economic_implication: Avoids duplicate manual control operation in year 1 [E]
financial_control_implication: Sampled manual check retains a detective control
acceptance_criteria: Given the first observation period, then each key control has generated evidence with IPE support and a sampled manual re-performance; the auditor's planned approach records whether it relies on generated evidence

original_purpose: No production dependency under non-commercial terms
problem: Correct gate, but with no published Echelon commercial terms it blocks commercial entry without a dated decision or cost cap
proposed_replacement: Require, by architecture acceptance, either an executed commercial licence with escrow/fork right and a priced, arm's-length related-party agreement, or a costed replacement plan (plain CSS/print) that keeps release 1 free of PolyForm NC components; record the decision date
economic_implication: Bounds licence cost (T01 cost-plus $129-668k/yr [D]) or replacement cost
acceptance_criteria: Given architecture acceptance, then the SBOM licence check passes and the licence or replacement plan has a recorded price and owner

problem: Requires a 12-month shadow replay and a 90-day time study at a real sponsor before any segment commitment, which presupposes a sponsor willing to engage without commitment
proposed_replacement: Permit a design-partner contract before measurement if it has a price collar, a measurement milestone (90-day time study + shadow replay) and a stop-loss/exit for both parties; keep the ban on public economic claims until measured
economic_implication: Allows staged revenue and prepaid implementation; caps downside
acceptance_criteria: Given a design-partner contract, then price adjusts within the collar after the time study and either party may exit at the milestone with defined costs

problem: Schema/role per sponsor in production is justified, but per-sponsor sandboxes and per-tenant configuration environments add ~$12k per sponsor-year and per-tenant migration work
proposed_replacement: Keep schema-per-tenant in production; default non-production to a shared environment with synthetic tenants and replayed anonymised data; dedicated sandbox only by contract; fleet migrations automated (CNV-ARC-005)
economic_implication: ~$6-12k per sponsor-year less [D from CST-T06]
security_implication: Synthetic data reduces PII in non-prod
acceptance_criteria: Given a new sponsor, then onboarding uses the shared sandbox unless the contract requires otherwise, and no production PII exists outside production

problem: Every material change needs affirmative adoption by each sponsor; platform-maintained regulatory content (data-format changes, list updates) multiplies handoffs by sponsor count
proposed_replacement: Classify changes: platform-maintained regulatory content and non-substantive updates adopted under a standing pre-authorisation with notice and an opt-out window; eligibility, financial-control, permission and customer-rights changes keep affirmative adoption and independent approval
economic_implication: Handoffs scale with change classes, not sponsors x changes
financial_control_implication: Independent approval retained for material changes
acceptance_criteria: Given a non-substantive regulatory-content change, then each sponsor receives notice and the change applies after the window unless opted out; given a material change, then affirmative adoption is required

problem: Release 1 limits agent execution to reversible internal A2 actions, so sending approved-template status messages, document requests and evidence refreshes require a human click
problem_category: restricts appropriate AI; creates recurring human work
proposed_replacement: Add an enumerated list of external but reversible or low-impact actions an agent may execute under deterministic guards (approved templates, rate limits, sampling): status notices, document requests, evidence refresh, bank-detail verification requests; reserved decisions stay human
economic_implication: Removes clicks on high-volume low-risk actions [E]
security_implication: Prompt-injection risk handled by deterministic dossier sections (CNV-AIO-002)
acceptance_criteria: Given an agent-sent status notice, then the template id, guard results and sampled review are recorded; no agent can execute a reserved or money-moving action

original_purpose: Prevent insider or erroneous changes to control-relevant code
problem: Two human approvers (neither the author) on every change needs at least three engineers for every control-relevant change; with a single human maintainer and agent authors this forces conventional staffing
proposed_replacement: Risk-tier diffs: author (human or agent) + one independent human + mandatory automated verification (property tests, mutation score threshold, invariant checks, signed provenance) for low-risk diffs; two humans for high-risk diffs (ledger posting rules, release gate, authority)
economic_implication: Avoids ~1 engineer at R (~$189k) if accepted
financial_control_implication: ITGC change-management design must be accepted by the auditor
acceptance_criteria: Given a diff classified low-risk, then merge requires one human approver plus all automated gates green and provenance signed; misclassification rate measured by sampled re-review below an agreed bound
remaining_uncertainty: No evidence automated verification substitutes for a second reviewer; may be worse

problem: The 90-day time study is designed as a study, i.e. a manual measurement project
problem_category: prevents automated control evidence; prevents workload-driven operations
proposed_replacement: Instrument the work queue so handling time, touches and exception classes are captured automatically from day one (event log), with a manual calibration sample; the time study becomes a continuous metric
economic_implication: Lower measurement cost; continuous evidence
acceptance_criteria: Given 90 days of operation, then the event log yields minutes per exception class with a calibration sample error under an agreed bound

problem: Attribution starts from provider invoices; related-party engineering time (Echelon, founders) is not metered, so shared Echelon resources can look free
proposed_replacement: Extend x_Bearer to intercompany and founder-time bearers; map work-item telemetry hours to cost objects at loaded cost; show related-party licence and service charges separately
economic_implication: No cost change; prevents understatement (A layer $0.43M/yr fully allocated at R [D])
acceptance_criteria: Given a month, then attribution reconciles invoices plus intercompany charges and the showback lists Echelon hours by cost object

problem: Pre-delegation duration is a modelled parameter, not a commercial condition; sponsors that never delegate keep the servicer at AI-enhanced cost
proposed_replacement: Make delegation readiness a sales qualification and price term: a pre-delegation surcharge or time-limited pre-delegation period in the contract
economic_implication: Caps the ~$0.94M/yr reversion exposure at R [M]
acceptance_criteria: Given a contract, then it states the pre-delegation period and the fee that applies if delegation is not adopted by its end
legal_obligation_preserved: yes: delegation stays a board act

problem: Full history import with reconciliation for every fund drives the $75k (25-250k) migration line per sponsor
proposed_replacement: Migrate active state and opening balances fully with reconciliation; import closed history as an immutable, searchable archive with document links and retention class, reconciled at totals rather than line-by-line
economic_implication: Lower migration cost per sponsor [E]
acceptance_criteria: Given a migrated sponsor, then active balances reconcile to the penny, archived history reconciles at fund-year totals and is retrievable for the retention period

problem: Register exists as a requirement but not as an executable, costed list; convention-only steps can persist unnoticed
proposed_replacement: Make the justification register machine-readable with measured minutes per step, cost per year and review date; quarterly generated report of human steps by justification class
economic_implication: Makes removal decisions evidence-based
financial_control_implication: Keeps legal/fiduciary steps visible as non-removable
acceptance_criteria: Given a quarter, then every human step in production has a justification class, measured minutes and an owner; steps past review date are flagged

problem: Monthly controller sign-off and 100% review per new source for a full close cycle per sponsor
proposed_replacement: Controller signs an automatically generated completeness certificate (populations, matched counts, break aging, sample results) rather than assembling it; new-source calibration reused per feed format (RC-ACT-005)
economic_implication: Lower controller hours per sponsor [E]
acceptance_criteria: Given month-end, then a completeness certificate with IPE support exists before sign-off and the controller's sign-off references it
